<issue>
Missing required IEnumerable argument causes runtime error
If an `IEnumerable` type argument is defined, the error message "Required argument missing for command" will not be shown; instead, it will directly throw an error.

```
Argument<string[]> argument = new("test argument");
RootCommand rootCommand = new RootCommand("Test") { argument };
rootCommand.SetAction(result => Console.WriteLine(result.GetRequiredValue(argument)));
await rootCommand.Parse(args).InvokeAsync();
```
If you run the example above, an error will occur.

```
Unhandled exception: System.InvalidOperationException: test argument is required but was not provided.
   at System.CommandLine.Parsing.SymbolResult.GetRequiredValue[T](Argument`1 argument)
   at System.CommandLine.ParseResult.GetRequiredValue[T](Argument`1 argument)
   at Program.<>c__DisplayClass0_0.<<Main>$>b__0(ParseResult result) in D:\Dev\Study\ConsoleApp1\Program.cs:line 5
   at System.CommandLine.Command.<>c__DisplayClass30_0.<SetAction>b__0(ParseResult context)
   at System.CommandLine.Invocation.AnonymousSynchronousCommandLineAction.Invoke(ParseResult parseResult)
   at System.CommandLine.Invocation.InvocationPipeline.InvokeAsync(ParseResult parseResult, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
```
If the `Argument` is changed to `string`, no error will occur.

My English is not very good, so I used an AI translator. Please let me know if I haven't expressed myself clearly.

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (System.CommandLine), find where "Required argument missing for command" error is produced (likely in src/System.CommandLine/Parsing/CommandResult.cs or ParseResult / ArgumentResult / Validate). Print relevant code with line numbers, including how arity / MinimumNumberOfValues and implicit/default arity for IEnumerable arguments is determined (Argument.cs, ArgumentArity).

content.content: {"summary":"The command error text is 'Required argument '{0}' missing for command: '{1}'.' (the repo has no literal 'Required argument missing for command'). It is raised from two places: CommandResult.ValidateArgumentsAndAddDefaultResults and ArgumentArity.Validate. Both build the message through LocalizationResources.RequiredArgumentMissing. Default arity comes from ArgumentArity.Default.","findings":["Resource string: src/System.CommandLine/Properties/Resources.resx:135-137 (CommandRequiredArgumentMissing = \"Required argument '{0}' missing for command: '{1}'.\"). The option variant is at resx:138-139: \"Required argument missing for option: '{0}'.\"","src/System.CommandLine/LocalizationResources.cs:55-60: RequiredArgumentMissing(ArgumentResult) uses the command message when argumentResult.Parent is CommandResult. It fills in argument HelpName ?? Name and commandResult.IdentifierToken.Value. Otherwise it calls the OptionResult overload (line 65).","src/System.CommandLine/Parsing/CommandResult.cs:~146-176: ValidateArgumentsAndAddDefaultResults. When no ArgumentResult exists for an argument and (HasDefaultValue || Arity.MinimumNumberOfValues > 0), it creates one. If !HasDefaultValue and Min > 0, it calls argumentResult.AddError(LocalizationResources.RequiredArgumentMissing(argumentResult)) at line 168 and continues. When completeValidation is false, arguments without a default value are skipped.","src/System.CommandLine/ArgumentArity.cs:~76-117: static Validate(ArgumentResult, out error). It returns true if Parent is null or an implicit OptionResult. If Tokens.Count < Arity.MinimumNumberOfValues, it returns an ArgumentConversionResult.Failure with RequiredArgumentMissing (line 90) and type FailedMissingArgument. If tokenCount > Max and the parent is an option that does not allow multiple arguments per token, it fails with ExpectsOneArgument.","src/System.CommandLine/ArgumentArity.cs:140-170: Default(Argument, SymbolNode? firstParent). Boolean returns ZeroOrOne. A non-string IEnumerable type returns ZeroOrMore (0..100000) if the parent is a Command, otherwise OneOrMore (1..100000). If the parent is a Command and the argument HasDefaultValue or the type is nullable, it returns ZeroOrOne. Anything else returns ExactlyOne (1,1). MaximumArity = 100_000 (line 21).","src/System.CommandLine/ArgumentArity.cs:~60: IsNonDefault is set only by the explicit constructor. Equals and GetHashCode include it.","src/System.CommandLine/Argument.cs:32-44: the Arity getter computes ArgumentArity.Default(this, FirstParent) lazily while _arity.IsNonDefault is false. The setter assigns _arity directly."],"confidence":0.9}
